newsitem.title: USA: Nissan sees slightly higher U.S. sales.
newsitem.headline: Nissan sees slightly higher U.S. sales.

text.p: Nissan Motor Corp U.S.A. expects to sell slightly more cars and light trucks in the United States out of its Nissan Division in 1997, a top executive said Thursday.

Thomas Eastwood, vice president of sales for the Nissan Division, said at an Automotive Press Association gathering that 1998 sales for the unit are expected to rise 8-9 percent, or to about 760,000 units. Last year, Nissan Division's U.S. sales were about 700,000 units.
Nissan Motor Corp U.S.A. is a unit of Nissan Motor Co Ltd.
The Japanese automaker set pricing for its 1998 Altima car line at the APA session. The high-volume model 1998 Altima GXE was priced at $17,990, excluding a $470 destination charge.
Eastwood said he expects 1998-model-year Altima U.S. retail sales to be 155,000 vehicles. He said total U.S. 1998-model-year Altima sales are expected to be 170,000 vehicles.
Eastwood said another 20,000 of the cars will be sold in Canada and other U.S. territories.
Annual Altima capacity at Nissan's Smyrna, Tenn., plant is about 200,000 vehicles.
